title: LDAEP and resting-state EEG in healthy women
description: This dataset comprises resting-state and loudness dependence of auditory evoked potentials (LDAEP) EEG recordings from 69 healthy women (ages 19-40 years) acquired at the University of Oslo. The study investigates the relationship between hormonal contraceptive use and central serotonergic activity indexed by LDAEP. Data include 64-channel EEG recordings at 2048 Hz sampling rate, alongside comprehensive phenotypic data on hormonal contraceptive use, menstrual cycle phase, depressive symptoms, impulsivity, and lifestyle factors.
methods_description: EEG data were recorded using a BioSemi ActiveTwo system with 64 Ag-AgCl electrodes positioned according to the extended 10-20 system (10-10) at 2048 Hz sampling rate. Two paradigms were recorded per participant: resting-state (4 minutes eyes-closed followed by 4 minutes eyes-open; n=69) and LDAEP (1000 Hz tones at five intensity levels: 55, 65, 75, 85, and 95 dB SPL with 80 trials per level; n=54). Four auxiliary oculogram channels (HOG1, HOG2, VOG1, VOG2) were positioned near the outer canthi and above/below the right eye. Raw data were stored in BrainVision format with standard software anti-aliasing filtering applied.
